subject: Close runway drift — proposed rebaseline, MAP update, and escalation
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morozova <elena@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan@dataflow.io>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Close runway drift — propose rebaseline & MAP update

Elena / Jordan,

Quick note following our Friday call — thank you for the transparency on the internal eval schedule. Based on the new dates you shared (security review moved to 6/15 and integration testing to 6/22), the close date we previously had (6/30) is at material risk.

I attached an updated MAP (MAP_v3.xlsx) and a short snapshot of our risk log. Key points:
- Security/infosec gating shifted by ~2 weeks (SOC evidence handoff now 6/10).
- Integration test window compressed; Dataflow needs an additional day for the connector sandbox.
- Procurement sign-off timeline appears unchanged but is dependent on the risk acceptance memo.

Proposed immediate next steps from Redwood:
1) Officially rebaseline the mutual action plan to a target close of 7/14 to give a conservative buffer.
2) Deliver a prioritized remediation playbook for the integration blocker by 05/20.
3) Schedule a one-hour executive sync (REDWOOD PM + ACME Procurement + ACME InfoSec) this week to agree on the new date and acceptance criteria.

Can you confirm whether ACME can accept a formal MAP rebaseline to 7/14 and if Jordan can be the engineering POC for the connector adjustments? If you prefer a different date, tell us now so we can model impact to commit and capacity.

Thanks,
Mike
Michael Grant
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
michael@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123
Redwood Inference

Attachments: MAP_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet), risk_log_snapshot_20260518.csv (CSV)
From: Elena Morozova <elena@acme-corp.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Close runway drift — propose rebaseline & MAP update

Mike,

Thanks for the clear summary and the files. I ran this by procurement and infosec this morning:
- InfoSec: SOC evidence handoff is likely to be 6/11 now (they need an extra week to validate our internal vendor questionnaire).
- Engineering (Jordan): can shift the sandbox parity work but needs until 6/18 to get a stable connector build.
- Procurement: would prefer to keep paperwork rolling but won't sign until infosec clears.

Given those inputs, I agree a conservative target of 7/14 is reasonable. We want a short remediation-runbook itemized by priority so our InfoSec and Eng leads can sign off quickly.

I'll block time for the exec sync tomorrow at 10am PT and loop in our procurement lead if needed. Jordan is copied on the calendar invite.

Elena
Elena Morozova
Sr. Director, Cloud Platform — Acme Corp
elena@acme-corp.com

From: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, connor_obrien <connor@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Morozova <elena@acme-corp.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan@dataflow.io>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: INTERNAL — ACME rebaseline approval & escalation steps

Team —

Following Elena's confirmation, ACME is provisionally OK with a 7/14 target. Per the MAP and our risk log, we need to lock three mitigations now or we'll see further slip:

Top immediate actions (owner & ETA):
- Connector sandbox priority patch (Connor) — deliver testable build by 2026-06-12.
- SOC artifacts bundle (Neha) — compile and deliver vendor evidence package to ACME by 2026-06-09.
- Procurement acceleration play (Laura) — share expedited contract checklist and draft SOW addendum by 2026-06-02 so Acme's procurement can pre-clear terms.

Risk positions and contingency:
- If connector fails validation on first pass, plan to open a scoped fallback: limited feature set cutover (tokens throttling + reduced context) to allow a soft launch on 7/14.
- If SOC artifacts slip beyond 6/12, escalate to Bryan (VP Sales) for desktop credits & temporary SLA concessions.

Ask: I need confirmation from each owner by EOD tomorrow that the ETAs are achievable. I will draft a short MAP addendum for signature after we validate dates.

Thanks — Mike

--
Michael Grant
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morozova <elena@acme-corp.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan@dataflow.io>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, connor_obrien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Close runway drift — proposed rebaseline & MAP update (Updated MAP + exec sync notes)

Elena / Jordan —

Thanks again for the exec sync this morning. As discussed, attached is the MAP addendum and a 1-page remediation playbook we committed to during the call. Summary of decisions:
- New target close: 2026-07-14 (mutually accepted).
- Acceptance criteria: Integration smoke test green, SOC artifacts bundle accepted by InfoSec, procurement sign-off on SOW addendum.
- Contingency: soft-launch feature flag if connector validation requires a small follow-up patch.

Immediate deliverables we own: MAP addendum (signed), connector build for sandbox (6/12), SOC bundle (6/09), SOW addendum draft (6/02). Attached: EvalChecklist_v2.pdf (test cases + pass/fail gating) and the MAP_v3.xlsx with the updated milestones.

Please reply with a short confirmation on the roadmap items so we can check the box for ACME's procurement. If anything changes on ACME's side, we will update the risk log and alert your procurement lead immediately.

Appreciate the collaboration — Mike

Attachments: MAP_v3.xlsx, EvalChecklist_v2.pdf
